meta.name: AI Roulette
meta.purpose: Show a commercial leader where the business needs to be in 12 months, what is in the way, and roughly what that gap is costing them, in their own numbers, with one practical move to make next.
meta.promise: Where could your pipeline be in 12 months, what's in the way, and what is it costing you?
meta.pov: AI fails in commercial work when it is done fast, without governance, on work that doesn't matter.
meta.referenceFrame: Answer for the commercial work you know: winning work (auctions, tenders, bids and applications), getting projects through procurement to a decision, and handing work into delivery. Think about the last six months. Some statements are about the work itself, not AI. That is deliberate: AI can only run on work that is clear enough to carry it. If you don't know, choose Not sure. It doesn't count against you.
meta.honestLabel: Your view of the commercial work you know.
meta.disclaimer: An indicative self-assessment of your view of the commercial work you know. Not a benchmark or an audit. Cost figures are your own estimates, multiplied out; we add no industry averages.

audience.primary: Founder or CEO of a fund-backed, growth-stage renewables IPP or developer (50 to 300 staff; solar and BESS, onshore wind and hybrids, offshore including floating; UK and Ireland, France, Iberia).
audience.direction: CEOs, MDs and commercial, development or BD directors who decide where effort and money go.
audience.practice: Bid, development, procurement, commercial and contract managers who do the work and see how AI is really used.
audience.also: Other commercial leaders in energy, infrastructure and industrial businesses, via the sector tap.

meta.sectorNote: The sector tap changes example wording only (textBySector, labelBySector, helpBySector, moveBySector). Questions, options, order and scoring are identical for every sector. 'ipp' is the default wording and the fallback when a sector variant is missing.

flow.endCapture: CTA depends on private urgency: Need -> 'Talk it through, 20 minutes' (Calendly) primary; Maybe or Want -> 'Get the full report' (email) primary.

packs.title: Energy developers: where you could be in 12 months
Industrial businesses: where you could be in 12 months

meta.packNote: A pack changes the landing pack line and the result bridge, and preselects the sector tap (the user can still change it). Questions and scoring never change by pack. URLs: Yorik to supply.
meta.changesFromV3: Vision step added (V1, unscored). Sector tap added (X2, wording only). Gap cut from 9 levers x 3 statements (27) to 6 levers x 2 statements (12); one positive and one reverse item per lever. Maturity cut from 5 to 2 (M1, M3). Cost cut from 6 to 5 (K5 retired; K4 still skipped when K3 = None). 30-day urgency test added (U1, scored privately as need, maybe or want). Result shows score, biggest gap, cost and one move, and routes to the Ignis path (Map the opportunity, Design the model, Support delivery).

groups.question: Is AI aimed at the work that decides your year?
groups.blurb: Whether AI is pointed at the outcomes that matter, such as the next auction or an FID date, and whether you know what the gap is worth.

levers.name: Focus
levers.question: Is AI aimed at the outcomes that decide your year?
levers.description: Whether AI effort is concentrated on one or two named commercial outcomes, such as the next auction submission or weeks to FID, each with a measure.
levers.costLine: Effort spreads across trials while the bottlenecks that decide whether you win the slot or reach FID on time get no focused help.
levers.bridge: Where you want to be in 12 months needs a first target. Name the one outcome AI should move, and stop the rest.

archetype.name: The Magpie
archetype.oneLiner: Every new AI tool gets a trial. No commercial outcome gets a priority.
archetype.headline: You have more AI activity than AI direction, so nothing gets enough attention to change a result.
archetype.stuck: Tool demos, licences and side projects keep arriving, and each looks promising. Because nobody has named the one or two outcomes AI should move first, such as the next auction submission or the FID date on a lead project, effort spreads thin, pilots never finish, and the board hears about tools rather than results.
moves: List every live AI trial on one page, with the outcome each is meant to move.
Pick one outcome tied to a date, such as the next auction submission or a lead project's FID, and pause trials that don't serve it.
Give the surviving use an owner, a measure and a 30-day decision date.

moveBySector.ipp: Pick one outcome with a date on it, such as your next auction submission or a lead project's FID, and pause every AI trial that doesn't serve it.
moveBySector.epc: Pick one outcome with a date on it, such as your next major tender submission, and pause every AI trial that doesn't serve it.
moveBySector.oem: Pick one outcome with a date on it, such as the next big supply tender or quote turnaround, and pause every AI trial that doesn't serve it.
moveBySector.services: Pick one outcome with a date on it, such as the next framework or major contract bid, and pause every AI trial that doesn't serve it.
moveBySector.other: Pick one commercial outcome with a date on it and pause every AI trial that doesn't serve it.

warningSigns: Your team has tried more AI tools this year than it can name results from.
Different leaders give different answers to 'what is AI for here?'
Pilots end with 'interesting' rather than a decision.
archetype.strongLine: You know what AI is for. Every other fix gets easier because of it.
archetype.success: Anyone on the leadership team gives the same answer to 'what should AI improve first?'

perspective.direction: Decide the one outcome AI must move this year, and stop funding trials that don't serve it.
perspective.practice: Ask your director which outcome AI is for, and bring one use that serves it.

levers.name: Value case
levers.question: Do you know what the gap is worth?
levers.description: Whether AI is judged on commercial results, such as auctions won, FID dates protected or margin, rather than hours saved.
levers.costLine: Without a known cost of a month's slip, the uses that protect revenue and programme dates never get funded, and the ones that do can't prove their worth to the board.
levers.bridge: To close the gap to where you want to be, you need to know what each month of it costs. That number decides what gets funded.

archetype.name: The Builder
archetype.oneLiner: It could probably work. Nobody has put a number on what it's worth.
archetype.headline: You are investing in AI before anyone has shown what result it should change, or what that result is worth.
archetype.stuck: AI cases count hours saved because that is easy to measure. What a month's slip to FID, a missed auction round or a lost grid slot costs is rarely written down, so AI is judged on activity and gets trimmed in the next budget round.
moves: Put a rough number on what one month's slip costs on a typical project. Your finance team can do it in a day.
Express your leading AI use in those terms, not hours saved.
Stop any AI spend that cannot name the result it should change.

moveBySector.ipp: Ask finance for a rough figure for what one month's slip to FID costs on a typical project, and judge every AI use against it, not hours saved.
moveBySector.epc: Ask finance for a rough figure for what a month's delay to a tender award or project start costs, and judge every AI use against it, not hours saved.
moveBySector.oem: Ask finance for a rough figure for what a month's delay to a major order costs, and judge every AI use against it, not hours saved.
moveBySector.services: Ask finance for a rough figure for what a month's delay to a contract award or mobilisation costs, and judge every AI use against it, not hours saved.
moveBySector.other: Ask finance for a rough figure for what a month of delay costs on typical work, and judge every AI use against it, not hours saved.

warningSigns: Business cases count hours saved, not revenue, margin or time to decision.
Nobody knows what a month's slip costs.
No AI initiative has ever been stopped for falling short.
archetype.strongLine: You know what the gap is worth. That discipline protects every other bet.
archetype.success: Your leading AI use has a measure in money or time, and a date to decide whether it continues.

perspective.direction: Refuse any AI spend without a measure in money or time and a decision date.
perspective.practice: Put rough numbers on your best AI use: time or money before and after.

levers.name: Reusable evidence
levers.question: Can you find, trust and reuse your best evidence?
levers.description: Whether your best evidence, answers and expert judgement can be found, trusted and reused, by people and by AI, rather than living in a few heads and old folders.
levers.costLine: Hours of rework on every submission and data room request, inconsistent claims across bids, and hard questions queuing behind the same few people.
levers.bridge: Where you want to be in 12 months will draw on what you already know. Make it findable before you ask AI to use it.

archetype.name: The Reinventor
archetype.oneLiner: Good work gets done once, then quietly redone.

card.strength: Your team can write anything from scratch.

archetype.headline: You have already written your best answers, and your experts already know the hard ones. Neither is easy to reuse.
archetype.stuck: Track record, supply chain plans, grid and consenting answers and lender Q&A sit across inboxes, data rooms and old folders with no owner, and judgement lives in a few heads. Teams rewrite rather than reuse, and AI drawing on that mess gives confident answers from the wrong version.
moves: Pick the twenty answers or documents you reuse most and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.
Ask your two most-asked people to record one judgement they make every time, as a checklist with worked examples.
Point AI only at that approved set and measure time to first draft.

moveBySector.ipp: Pick the twenty pieces of evidence you reuse most across auctions, lender packs and data rooms, and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.
moveBySector.epc: Pick the twenty method statements, case studies and answers you reuse most in tenders, and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.
moveBySector.oem: Pick the twenty technical, quality and compliance answers you reuse most in quotes and tenders, and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.
moveBySector.services: Pick the twenty case studies and answers you reuse most in bids, and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.
moveBySector.other: Pick the twenty answers or documents you reuse most and keep one approved, dated version of each in one place.

warningSigns: Finding last year's best answer takes longer than rewriting it.
The same two or three people get asked every hard question.
Two submissions have gone out with different versions of the same claim.
archetype.strongLine: Your best evidence and judgement are findable and reusable. That is what makes AI output worth trusting.
archetype.success: Anyone can find the current, approved answer to a common question in minutes.

perspective.direction: Fund one owner and one approved library for the evidence you reuse most.
perspective.practice: Save your best answer from this month where others, and AI, can find it.

levers.name: Handover
levers.question: Do commitments survive the move into procurement and delivery?
levers.description: Whether what you commit to while developing and winning a project reaches the people who procure, finance and deliver it.
levers.costLine: Surprises at procurement, lender due diligence or delivery, rework on EPC and supply terms, and dates that slip after the decision that should have fixed them.
levers.bridge: Where you want to be in 12 months has to be delivered, not just won. Carry every commitment across, or the gains leak at handover.

archetype.name: The Sprinter
archetype.oneLiner: You win at pace, then the next team starts from a blank page.
archetype.headline: The thinking that won the project doesn't make it across the handover.
archetype.stuck: Consent conditions, grid terms, auction commitments and assumptions agreed during development live in documents and heads the procurement and delivery teams never see. The thread breaks exactly where margin, lender confidence and the FID date are won or lost.
moves: For your last win, list every commitment, assumption and risk made to win it.
Check how many of them the procurement or delivery team knew about at the start.
Make a commitments register a required item at every handover.

moveBySector.ipp: For your most recent auction award or consented project, list every commitment made to win it, then check how many the EPC and turbine or module procurement team knew about.
moveBySector.epc: For your last tender win, list every commitment made to win it, then check how many the site and delivery team knew about at mobilisation.
moveBySector.oem: For your last major order, list every commitment made to win it, then check how many production and delivery knew about at kick-off.
moveBySector.services: For your last contract win, list every commitment made to win it, then check how many the delivery team knew about at mobilisation.
moveBySector.other: For your last win, list every commitment made to win it, then check how many the delivery team knew about at the start.

warningSigns: Procurement or delivery teams discover commitments after the decision.
Handover is a meeting, not a record.
Lenders' advisers find things your own team didn't know.
archetype.strongLine: Your commitments survive the handover. That is where margin and dates are protected.
archetype.success: Every commitment in a live project can be traced to the decision behind it.

perspective.direction: Make handover a governed record, not a meeting.
perspective.practice: List the commitments in your last win and check which ones the next team knew about.

levers.name: Rules and checks
levers.question: Is AI used within clear rules, and checked before anyone relies on it?
levers.description: Whether people know which tools and information they may use with AI, and whether AI-assisted output is checked against its sources before it reaches a board, lender, assessor or client.
levers.costLine: One wrong figure in an auction submission, lender pack or board paper can cost more trust than a year of time savings earns, and can add weeks of questions.
levers.bridge: Where you want to be in 12 months only works if people trust what AI produces. Trust comes from rules and checks, not from how well it reads.

archetype.name: The Rubber Stamp
archetype.oneLiner: AI output goes out on a nod, not on evidence.

card.now: Now give it rules and evidence.

archetype.headline: If it reads well, it ships, and that is exactly when AI is most dangerous.
archetype.stuck: People are not sure which tools or information they may use, so the careful ones avoid AI and the confident ones use whatever they like. AI-assisted content reaches assessors, lenders and the board after a skim, not a check against sources, and nobody can show where an answer came from.
moves: Write a one-page 'what's allowed' guide covering information, tools and uses.
Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content that leaves the business.
Log AI errors in one place and use them to fix the process each month.

moveBySector.ipp: Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content going into an auction submission, lender pack or board paper, starting with the next one.
moveBySector.epc: Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content going into a tender or prequalification, starting with the next one.
moveBySector.oem: Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content going into a quote or tender, starting with the next one.
moveBySector.services: Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content going into a bid or client report, starting with the next one.
moveBySector.other: Require a named reviewer and a source check for any AI-assisted content that leaves the business, starting with the next one.

warningSigns: Some people use personal AI tools for work.
AI output that 'looks right' goes out without a source check.
You can't show what an AI answer was based on.
archetype.strongLine: People know the rules, and you verify before you rely. That is what makes AI safe to scale.
archetype.success: Every AI-assisted submission has a named reviewer and visible sources, and anyone can say what they may put into AI tools.

perspective.direction: Publish a one-page 'what's allowed' guide and require named review on anything AI-assisted that leaves the business.
perspective.practice: Add a source check to your own review step and raise the questions about what's allowed that nobody can answer.

levers.name: Ownership and decision rights
levers.question: Does someone own AI, and is it clear what it may never decide?
levers.description: Whether each AI-assisted process has a named owner and senior backing, and whether the decisions AI may inform but never make are written down.
levers.costLine: Problems linger, processes drift, and AI can't win budget or board confidence because nobody can show who answers for it.
levers.bridge: Where you want to be in 12 months needs someone senior to own it. Without an owner, the gap stays open by default.

archetype.name: The Bystander
archetype.oneLiner: Everyone uses it. Nobody owns it.

card.strength: AI is already in the work.
card.now: Now put a name on it.

archetype.headline: AI is everywhere in the work, and accountable nowhere.
archetype.stuck: No named person owns each AI-assisted process, nobody has written down what AI may never decide, and the board only sees AI use by asking around. When something goes wrong, deciding who fixes it becomes a meeting, and when the champion gets busy, progress stops.
moves: List the AI-assisted processes in regular use and name one owner for each.
Write down the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a bid price or a go/no-go.
Review your top AI priority at a senior level every quarter, against its measure.

moveBySector.ipp: Write down, on one page, the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as an auction bid price, an EPC award or a go/no-go at FID, and name an owner for each AI-assisted process.
moveBySector.epc: Write down, on one page, the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a tender price or a risk allowance, and name an owner for each AI-assisted process.
moveBySector.oem: Write down, on one page, the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a price, a lead time or a warranty term, and name an owner for each AI-assisted process.
moveBySector.services: Write down, on one page, the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a price or a contract risk, and name an owner for each AI-assisted process.
moveBySector.other: Write down, on one page, the decisions AI may inform but never make, such as a price or a go/no-go, and name an owner for each AI-assisted process.

warningSigns: AI processes have users but no owner.
'Who is accountable?' has no fast answer.
Leaders learn about AI use by asking around.
archetype.strongLine: Every AI process has an owner and clear limits. That is what accountability looks like, and what a board wants to see.
archetype.success: For every AI process in use, anyone can name its owner and the decisions it must not make.

perspective.direction: Name an owner for every AI-assisted commercial process, write down what AI may never decide, and sponsor the top priority yourself.
perspective.practice: Ask who owns the AI process you rely on. If nobody does, propose a name.

questions.use: Scored privately into need, maybe or want (see urgency). Never shown to the user as a label or judgement. Drives which CTA is primary and is stored as ar_urgency.

scoring.leverHealthPct: round(sum(itemScore over ANSWERED items) / (6 * answeredItems) * 100). Not sure (0) is excluded from numerator and denominator.
scoring.lowVisibility: Each lever has 2 statements. If fewer than minAnsweredPerLever (2 of 2) are answered, health = null (shown grey: 'Not enough visibility'), counted at 50% in total and group scores, excluded from archetype, shadow, strongest and fix-first.
scoring.total: round(mean of the 6 lever fractions, low-visibility levers at 0.5) * 100) -> Gap score 0-100 (higher = smaller gap).
scoring.groupScores: Per group (aim, build, govern): round(mean of its 2 lever fractions * 100). weakestGroup = lowest, ties by group order.

bands.name: Spinning the wheel
bands.blurb: AI is happening, but it is not aimed, built in or governed. Results, good or bad, are mostly chance.
bands.climb: Pick one commercial outcome, give it an owner, and get your biggest gap out of the red.

bands.name: Placing bets
bands.tag: Some bets are smart. Not all are covered.
bands.blurb: You have real foundations in places, but gaps in aim, workflow or control mean wins are hard to repeat or scale.
bands.climb: Turn one promising use into an owned, checked part of the work with a measure, then extend it.

bands.name: Running the house
bands.blurb: AI is aimed at what matters, built into the work and governed. The job now is compounding: wider use, new value, tighter evidence.
bands.climb: Use your foundations to test one new AI-enabled service clients would pay for.

governanceGate.rule: If the band is 'house' and any answered govern lever has health < 40, cap the band at 'betting'. The number is unchanged. Low-visibility govern levers do not trigger the gate but appear in Blind spots.
governanceGate.message: Your score is high, but {lever} is in the red. AI that isn't governed can't be trusted at scale, so we've held your band at Placing bets.

scoring.archetype: Answered lever with the LOWEST health. Ties: lever order (aim before build before govern).
scoring.shadow: Second-lowest answered lever. noStrongShadow if fewer than 3 answered levers or health(3rd) - health(2nd) < shadowGapPts.
scoring.genericShadow: Your other levers are close together, so no single second gap stands out. Fixing your biggest gap will lift several at once.
scoring.strongest: Answered lever with the HIGHEST health. Ties: lever order.
scoring.fixFirst: Among answered red levers (<40), earliest group (aim, build, govern), then lowest health, then order. If none red, fixFirst = archetype. Rationale: the POV - aim AI at work that matters before scaling it.
scoring.straightLining: On answered gap items: if 10+ answered and population SD of raw answers < 0.5, show the 'did you answer quickly?' note. Never block.
scoring.straightLiningNote: Your answers were very similar across all statements. If you went quickly, your result may be less sharp than it could be. Retake any time.
scoring.visibilityOnly: If every lever is low visibility, show the Blind spots result only (no archetype).

blindSpots.rule: List levers with 1+ Not sure, most first (max 3).

copy.direction: You chose Not sure on {n} statements, mostly in {levers}. For a leader that is a finding in itself: these are the questions to ask your team this week.
copy.practice: You chose Not sure on {n} statements, mostly in {levers}. Ask your director how these work; the answer may surprise you both.

weakestGroupCopy.aim: Your gap sits mostly in Aim: AI isn't yet pointed at the work that decides your year.
weakestGroupCopy.build: Your gap sits mostly in Build in: AI hasn't become part of how the work runs.
weakestGroupCopy.govern: Your gap sits mostly in Govern: AI isn't yet controlled well enough to put in front of a board, lender or assessor.

scoring.acquiescence: Every lever has one positive and one reverse statement, so all-agree, all-disagree and all-neutral each score exactly 50.

cost.principle: Every figure is the respondent's own estimate multiplied out. No benchmarks, no industry averages, no win-rate assumptions. Ranges, not points. Open-ended top options show as 'X+'.

dimensions.label: Time
dimensions.question: K2
dimensions.line: About {lo} to {hi} hours a year spent searching for, rewriting or redoing work (roughly {fteLo} to {fteHi} full-time people).

dimensions.label: Delay
dimensions.question: K3,K4
dimensions.line: About {lo} to {hi} weeks of slippage a year, across {count} delayed submissions, milestones or decisions.

dimensions.label: Missed value
dimensions.question: K6
dimensions.line: {count} opportunities passed on for lack of capacity in the last 12 months.

assumptions.note: 46 working weeks a year and 1,725 hours per full-time person (46 x 37.5). Stated on the result; change here if Yorik prefers other conventions.

formulas.timeHours: K1.range x K2.range x workingWeeks  (lo x lo, hi x hi; hi = open if either is open)
formulas.delayWeeks: K3.range x K4.range; if K3 = None then 0 and K4 is skipped
formulas.missedValue: K6.range x ownNumber, when ownNumber.type = 'dealValue'. Labelled 'value of work you couldn't go for', not lost profit.
formulas.severity: time = K2.severity; delay = 0 if K3 = None, else mean(K3.severity, K4.severity); missed = K6.severity. Not sure -> null (shown as 'Not sure: worth finding out'). Risk is no longer a cost tile in v4 (K5 retired); risk shows through the Govern levers.
formulas.biggestCost: Highest severity > 0. Ties: the archetype lever's costDims first, then dimOrder.
formulas.costIndex: round(mean of non-null severities x 100). CRM/analytics only; never shown as a score.

paths.rule: 1) band = house (after the governance gate) -> support. 2) band = spinning -> map. 3) fixFirst lever in group aim -> map. 4) V1 = aiplan -> map. 5) otherwise (fixFirst in build or govern) -> design. If every lever is low visibility -> map.

map.label: Map the opportunity
map.line: Map the work, data, governance, systems and decision rights. Identify the priority opportunities, then leave with a commercially grounded AI strategy and roadmap.
map.why: Your biggest gap is about where AI is aimed and what it is worth, so the first step is to map the opportunity before building anything.

design.label: Design the model
design.line: Turn the priority into a governed model: the proposition, workflow, evidence, human responsibilities, data, controls and a build-ready pilot brief.
design.why: You know where AI should help. Your gap is in how the work runs or is governed, so the next step is to design the model it runs on.

support.label: Support delivery
support.line: Stay involved while an internal team or technology partner builds, tests and refines the system. Protect the commercial intent, test the pilot and guide adoption into use.
support.why: Your foundations are in place. The next step is getting one governed use into live work and keeping the evidence tight while it scales.

routing.rule: Path (map, design, support) from paths.rule. CTA from urgency: need -> talk primary, report secondary; maybe or want -> report primary, talk secondary. Offer card: commercial-ai-adoption for every lever in v4.
